rules.notes: Cap sodium at <2300 mg/d for T2D. Loses to the stricter KDIGO 2000 mg/d ceiling when CKD is present (see CONFLICT-SODIUM-CKD-WINS).
rules.verbatim_quote: reduce sodium intake to less than 2,300 mg per day

rules.notes: Encourage 25-30 g/d dietary fibre; higher DASH fibre floor (30 g) wins for comorbid HTN.
rules.verbatim_quote: increase dietary fiber to 25-30 g per day

rules.notes: Saturated fat <10% of kcal; 22 g/d is the 2000-kcal reference. The absolute ceiling is recomputed by the engine from the energy target.
rules.verbatim_quote: limit saturated fat to less than 10% of total calories

rules.notes: No single macronutrient split is mandated; low-carbohydrate patterns (26-45% kcal) are an option. 130 g/d is the RDA floor for brain glucose.
rules.verbatim_quote: no single macronutrient distribution is recommended

rules.notes: For overweight/obese T2D, a 500 kcal/d deficit supports 5-10% weight loss. Recorded as an assert; optimiser may use as a soft objective.
In T2D without CKD, protein need is not reduced (approx. 1.0 g/kg/d). Suppressed by the CKD protein ceiling when CKD is present.

actions.reason: SSBs drive glycaemic load; prefer water or unsweetened drinks.

rules.notes: Exclude sugar-sweetened beverages.
Favour low-GI, high-fibre carbohydrate sources.
Baseline DASH sodium ceiling for HTN. Overridden by the KDIGO 2000 mg/d ceiling when CKD is present.
rules.verbatim_quote: reduce sodium intake to less than 2,300 mg per day

rules.notes: Ideal sodium target ~1500 mg/d (greater BP reduction). A target, not a hard ceiling; the CKD ceiling remains the binding hard limit.
rules.verbatim_quote: an ideal target of less than 1,500 mg per day

rules.notes: DASH recommends ~4700 mg/d potassium from food for HTN. Contradicted by CKD/hyperkalaemia: suppressed by CONFLICT-K-DASH-VS-CKD and CKD-2024-POTASSIUM-INDIV.
rules.verbatim_quote: increase dietary potassium to 3,500-5,000 mg per day

rules.notes: DASH emphasises fruit, vegetables, whole grains; 30 g/d fibre floor is stricter than the ADA 25 g floor.
DASH saturated fat ~6% kcal; 13 g/d is the 2000-kcal reference and is stricter than the ADA 10% ceiling.
Weight reduction lowers BP; target >=5% loss when overweight.
DASH pattern: rich in fruits, vegetables, low-fat dairy, whole grains, nuts, lean protein; reduced saturated fat and cholesterol.
Limit alcohol as part of BP management.
KDIGO recommends <2000 mg/d sodium in CKD; stricter than ADA/DASH 2300, so CKD wins the sodium conflict.
rules.verbatim_quote: recommend sodium intake less than 2 g per day

rules.notes: Protein 0.55-0.8 g/kg/d for CKD stage 3-4 (not on dialysis). Engine scales the per-kg coefficient by patient weight into absolute grams in the envelope.
rules.verbatim_quote: maintain protein intake at 0.8 g/kg per day

rules.notes: Avoid high protein intake (>1.3 g/kg/d) in CKD. Safety ceiling; the stricter 0.8 g/kg CKD stage 3-4 max binds first.
Energy 25-35 kcal/kg/d to maintain nutritional status in CKD. Engine scales per kg into absolute kcal.
Do NOT blanket-restrict potassium in CKD with normal serum K. Restriction only on hyperkalaemia (see HYPERK-2024-POTASSIUM-2400). Overrides DASH potassium target.
rules.verbatim_quote: do not routinely restrict dietary potassium

rules.notes: Do not restrict phosphorus when serum phosphate is in range; individualise to labs. Restriction only on hyperphosphataemia.

actions.reason: Inorganic phosphate additives are highly bioavailable; avoid processed meats/colas.

rules.notes: Prefer whole foods; avoid phosphate additives.

actions.reason: KCl salt substitutes can precipitate hyperkalaemia in CKD.

rules.notes: Avoid potassium-based salt substitutes when serum K is elevated.
KDOQI 2020 concurs with 0.55-0.8 g/kg/d for non-dialysis CKD 3-5; reinforce the KDIGO protein envelope.
Derive CKD stage from eGFR: 30-59 = stage 3, 15-29 = stage 4. Stage 5/dialysis is out of scope (see SCOPE-DIALYSIS-EXCLUDE).
Serum K >=5.0 mEq/L triggers a potassium ceiling of ~2400 mg/d. Beats the DASH 4700 mg target (priority 85 > 70).
rules.verbatim_quote: restrict dietary potassium in hyperkalaemia

actions.reason: High-K foods (banana, orange juice, potato, tomato, coconut water) worsen hyperkalaemia.

rules.notes: Exclude high-potassium food categories while serum K is elevated.

actions.reason: KCl salt substitutes are contraindicated in hyperkalaemia.

rules.notes: Hard-exclude potassium chloride salt substitutes.
Flag for repeat potassium and clinician review; any K restriction is a clinical decision.
Serum phosphate >=4.5 mg/dL triggers a dietary phosphorus ceiling of ~800 mg/d.
rules.verbatim_quote: lower elevated serum phosphate toward the normal range

actions.reason: Inorganic phosphate additives are the priority target when phosphate is elevated.

rules.notes: Prioritise removing phosphate additives over whole-food phosphorus.
Flag for repeat phosphate and consider binder review with the clinician.
ACEi/ARB raise hyperkalaemia risk. Caution flag; does not itself set a ceiling — combine with labs and CKD.
On ACEi/ARB plus CKD, monitor potassium and avoid high-K diet even if serum K currently normal.

actions.value: maintain hydration; euglycaemic DKA risk with very-low-carb/keto and fasting

rules.notes: Informational: avoid very-low-carbohydrate/ketogenic patterns and prolonged fasting on SGLT2i.

actions.value: check B12; avoid excess alcohol; dose per eGFR

rules.notes: Informational: long-term metformin is associated with B12 deficiency; ensure B12-rich foods.
Loop/thiazide diuretics can cause hypokalaemia; do not apply a potassium ceiling without a supporting lab value.

actions.value: monitor serum potassium and creatinine after initiation or any dose change; assess dietary potassium

rules.notes: Cited medication-nutrient rule: RASi raises hyperkalaemia risk; KDIGO 2024 says hyperkalaemia on RASi can often be managed by measures to reduce serum potassium rather than decreasing the RASi dose, so dietary potassium is assessed (not blanket-restricted). Dataset vocabulary token is 'ACEi' (no ARB or generic drug names in the current cohort); generic spellings are accepted for forward compatibility. Coexists with MED-ACEI-ARB-K-CAUTION (unflagged caution) — this rule adds the cited monitoring instruction.
rules.verbatim_quote: Hyperkalemia associated with use of RASi can often be managed by measures to reduce the serum potassium levels rather than decreasing the dose

rules.section: Spironolactone and renin-angiotensin system drugs in heart failure

actions.value: ACEi/ARB + spironolactone: increased risk of potentially fatal hyperkalaemia and renal dysfunction; check serum potassium and renal function during the first and second week, then monthly for the first 2 months

rules.notes: Conjunction rule (two meds conditions are ANDed): RASi AND K-sparing diuretic co-prescription is a MHRA-flagged fatal-hyperkalaemia risk. No spironolactone in the current dataset cohort; the rule is inert for today's patients but guards future profiles.
rules.verbatim_quote: Recognised side effects of treatment with an ACEi or ARB include renal dysfunction and an increase in serum potassium

rules.guideline: KDIGO 2022 Diabetes Management in CKD Guideline

actions.value: review diuretic dose if hypovolaemia risk before or at SGLT2i initiation; hold SGLT2i during acute illness or fasting (sick-day rule)

rules.notes: Volume-depletion caution on SGLT2i initiation. No SGLT2i in the current dataset cohort; the token 'SGLT2i' matches the existing MED-SGLT2I-CONTEXT rule. Complements MED-SGLT2I-CONTEXT (hydration/euglycaemic-DKA context).
rules.verbatim_quote: If a patient is at risk for hypovolemia, consider decreasing thiazide or loop diuretic dosages before commencement of SGLT2i treatment

actions.value: monitor serum sodium and potassium on thiazide diuretics; individualised dietary potassium helps counter thiazide-induced hypokalaemia

rules.notes: Thiazide electrolyte monitoring. No thiazide in the current dataset cohort; the token 'thiazide' matches the existing MED-DIURETIC-K-LOSS rule. Dietary potassium stays individualised — this flag does NOT set a potassium target (that remains DASH/CKD/hyperkalaemia governed).
rules.verbatim_quote: Monitor for hyponatremia and hypokalemia, increased glucose, uric acid, and calcium levels.

rules.guideline: FDA Lasix label / 2025 AHA/ACC Hypertension Guideline

actions.value: monitor serum potassium and magnesium on loop diuretics (loop agents cause kaliuresis and magnesiuria)

rules.notes: Loop-diuretic K+/Mg monitoring. Token 'loop_diuretic' matches the example_trace patient and MED-DIURETIC-K-LOSS. Citation note: the verbatim_quote is verified from the 2025 AHA/ACC Hypertension Guideline (secondary source covering both thiazide-type and loop diuretics); no verbatim text is taken from the FDA Lasix label itself, which is cited as the primary interaction source.
rules.verbatim_quote: hypokalemia may be caused by kaliuresis from thiazide-type and loop diuretics

actions.value: take phosphate binders with each meal; doses taken without food do not bind dietary phosphate and are ineffective

rules.notes: Dataset vocabulary token is 'phosphate_binder' (P0005-P0007, P0014-P0016). Complements CKD-2024-PHOSPHATE-ADDITIVE (prefer_binders_with_meals assert): this rule adds the cited patient-facing timing instruction.
rules.verbatim_quote: binders should be given with meals as they limit gastrointestinal phosphate absorption

actions.value: keep vitamin K intake CONSISTENT week to week; do NOT avoid leafy greens; avoid drastic dietary changes while on warfarin

rules.notes: Consistency, not avoidance: the correct warfarin dietary instruction is a steady vitamin K intake. No warfarin in the current dataset cohort; the rule is inert for today's patients but guards future profiles and prevents an over-restrictive 'avoid vitamin K foods' interpretation.
rules.verbatim_quote: Eat a normal, balanced diet to maintain a consistent intake of vitamin K.

rules.guideline: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes 2026

actions.value: periodic vitamin B12 assessment with long-term metformin therapy, especially with anaemia or peripheral neuropathy

rules.notes: Dataset vocabulary token 'metformin' (P0001, P0003, P0004, P0010, P0012, P0013, P0019). Complements MED-METFORMIN-CONTEXT (check B12 context assert): this rule adds the cited ADA recommendation.
rules.verbatim_quote: Consider periodic assessment of vitamin B12 levels in individuals receiving long-term metformin therapy, especially in those with anemia or peripheral neuropathy.

rules.notes: Universal energy reference of 25-35 kcal/kg/d for ambulatory adults; scaled per kg by the engine.
Universal protein RDA floor 0.8 g/kg/d. Overridden by the CKD 0.55-0.8 envelope.
Universal fibre floor 25 g/d; stricter ADA/DASH floors win where applicable.
Baseline sodium ceiling when no higher-priority diagnosis applies.
Acceptable macronutrient distribution range for total fat: 20-35% kcal.
Free sugars <10% of energy as a general adult reference.

actions.reason: Pregnancy is out of CareLoop scope: nutrient needs and safety constraints differ and require obstetric oversight.

rules.notes: Hard scope exclusion. Any pregnancy flag removes the profile from CareLoop and escalates to a clinician.
CareLoop targets adults; paediatric profiles are out of scope.

CareLoop covers CKD stage 3-4 only. A dialysis / ESRD / CKD stage 5 diagnosis alone is out of scope regardless of any recorded eGFR (the eGFR may be missing or stale); it needs a renal dietitian. Lab-only detection of stage 5 is handled by SCOPE-EGFR-STAGE5-EXCLUDE.

Lab-only detection: a measured eGFR below 15 (CKD stage 5) is out of scope. An unknown eGFR never satisfies this rule (fail-safe guard); when a scope-class rule cannot be evaluated because a lab is missing, the engine records a scope_lab_unknown caution instead of silently skipping the gate.
Priority hierarchy CKD > HTN > T2D on sodium. Re-asserts the stricter CKD ceiling and records the resolution.

actions.value: potassium: CKD/hyperkalaemia restriction overrides DASH 4700 target

rules.notes: DASH potassium target (~4700 mg/d) is voided by CKD with hyperkalaemia. Restriction wins.

actions.value: potassium: no restriction; CKD with normal K does not adopt DASH 4700 target

rules.notes: DASH potassium target is not applied in CKD even when serum K is normal; no blanket restriction either.

INTERNAL SAFETY RULE (not from a public guideline; no external citation). Severe hyperkalaemia (serum K >= 5.5 mEq/L) tightens the potassium ceiling from 2400 to 2000 mg/d on top of HYPERK-2024-POTASSIUM-2400 and demands clinician review.

INTERNAL SAFETY RULE (not from a public guideline; no external citation). T2D with severely elevated HbA1c (>= 10%) is a ketoacidosis-risk presentation: the engine must not auto-propose a nutrient envelope; a clinician must review first.
